preamble: Shift of the palatalized alveolar stop [tʲ] to the palatal stop [c], with the secondary palatal articulation becoming the primary place. In Old Czech, the 13th-century depalatalization either merged soft consonants with their hard counterparts or turned them into the palatals ť, ď, ň.

examples.from: Old Czech soft t’ (e.g. in Proto-Slavic *tělo 'body')
examples.note: Palatalized t’ became the palatal stop ť [c], spelled t before ě and i.

sources: Wikipedia (2026). History of the Czech language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Czech_language
